name: Headlines at the top
what: The speaker's own words become big headlines at the top of the frame, one screen per phrase, each word on its onset.
when: On every phrase of a vertical short, for the whole short (no bottom subtitles).
why: Asked for big text at the top instead of timid subtitles; a verdict of the vertical-language review.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Words passing behind the speaker
what: The headlines sit on the under layer, so the head covers the part it rises into (person matte).
when: Every headline once the matte exists; each one goes through occlusion.mjs first.
why: Asked for text passing behind the speaker; kept through every pass.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Occlusion gate
what: Every headline word is measured against the head through the camera: 18 % hidden warns, 30 % refuses.
when: Before every render. The fix is a block moved or lifted, a word crossing the line above, or the word dropped, never a smaller word.
why: Keeps every word readable when the text goes behind the head.

name: Headlines laid on the room the head leaves
what: The space the head leaves free is measured phrase by phrase before the headlines are placed.
when: After matte.mjs, before writing the plan.
why: Measured, not guessed.

name: Impact with one Sacramento accent
what: Impact capitals for the words, the payoff in yellow, and one Sacramento script accent per screen written across the yellow word.
when: On every headline screen.
why: Asked for Impact in combination with a script face; Sacramento was liked after comparing.

name: Snell Roundhand or Lobster as the script face
what: Other script faces tried for the accent.
when: Never. Sacramento replaced them (Snell Roundhand stays only as a fallback when Sacramento is missing).
why: Compared and out: Snell Roundhand Black rejected as the secondary face, Lobster compared.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: One face per line
what: The script accent gets a line of its own above or below the Impact line, crossing it; the lines stack top to bottom, never side by side.
when: Always. line() warns when a line mixes the two faces.
why: Script and Impact side by side (« of using MY PLATFORM. ») was refused: it reads left to right, the rest of the short reads top to bottom.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Three headline placements
what: Seated: centred at y 0.17; holding something low: top-left, sliding behind the head; tight shot: below the head with anchor bottom at y 0.765 on the over layer.
when: Pick by the shot: seated, holding, or tight.
why: The numbers that made it work; all inside the feed's safe area.

name: Word pop and slam
what: A spring pop on each word (1.24 to 1), and a slam (1.9 to 1) for the one payoff of the minute.
when: Pop on every headline word; slam once a minute at most, on the payoff.

name: Shade over the top of the room
what: An edgeless dark gradient on the under layer, down to y 0.47, so the ceiling and window go into shadow behind the speaker and the white text holds.
when: Under the headlines on seated and holding shots; not on a tight shot with the words below the head.
why: Kept through the passes; replaced the blur band.

name: Blur band behind the text
what: The progressive blur band of the older subtitle layout.
when: Never in the vertical language (blurBand 0); shade() replaced it.
why: Belongs to the older subtitle layout.

name: Pro headlines (the explainer's light)
what: Every headline word with a two-layer shadow, yellow words glowing, a short blur on the pop, and a real exit that ends on the next screen's first word.
when: Always for the headlines over the speaker; the engine's plain headlines stay for the paper's subtitles only.
why: Asked for the polish of style 4: « très pro, style After Effects », keeping the paper.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Glitch drawn on one word
what: An RGB split and five torn slices over 0.22 s on the one word where the pack's glitch sounds.
when: Once, on the first yellow word of the hook.

name: Opening de-zoom
what: Every short opens on a de-zoom from 1.30 to 1.00 in 0.62 s, eased out, with a light whoosh.
when: At the start of every short.
why: Asked for: a light whoosh with a de-zoom at the start of every video.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Punch on an argument word
what: A quick zoom to 1.12-1.14 in 0.09-0.10 s, anchored on the eyes so the head grows downwards, released on the next phrase.
when: Only on a word that carries the argument.

name: Things coming out from behind the speaker
what: What the speaker names (a real capture, a real logo) starts inside their silhouette and slides out from behind them.
when: When the speaker names their product or a tool, and is not already showing it.
why: Asked to really play with the matte.

name: Logo chips from behind the head
what: A 400 px real logo comes out from behind the head with shutter motion blur, two shadows, a yellow glow, a gloss and a light swish.
when: One per thing said, no labels, no grid.

name: Orbit of logos round the head
what: Logos born behind the head that circle round it, half behind and half in front.
when: Never. Things come out from behind the speaker instead.
why: Refused as AI slop (generic AI filler), on the seventh version after six without a note.

name: Wall of big logos
what: Big logos landing one after another in front of the speaker, then behind.
when: Never.
why: Tried in place of the orbit and refused too.

name: No capture over a screen already shown
what: When the speaker holds a screen up to the camera, the screen is the picture: no capture slid over it.
when: Always: look at the shot first.
why: A capture over a shot where the speaker held the laptop up made no sense and was removed.

name: Matte holes
what: Cuts what the speaker holds (a laptop) out of the person matte, so it is not treated as the speaker.
when: When the speaker holds an object; before a screen emerges from behind them.
doc: plugins/video/references/pitfalls.md § What the speaker holds is not the speaker: matteHoles

name: Paper plate
what: A full-frame illustration on paper that drops over the shot; while it is up the headline steps down to discreet subtitles, Impact 66 px in ink.
when: For a full-frame illustration, about one graphic per 15-25 s of talking head.
why: Asked for the paper style, but not headlines on top of an illustration: both at once was too much.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Stop-motion on the paper
what: What is on the sheet enters at 8 poses a second, each pose held, never faded, each a little off by hand.
when: On the stickers and marks of every paper plate; the paper and its subtitles stay smooth.
why: Asked for movement on the paper, not smooth, few frames a second.

name: Real app icons as stickers with status marks
what: The real app icons as 360 px stickers on the paper, with felt marks in status colours (green, orange, yellow, red).
when: On a paper plate that names tools.
why: Kept through the passes without a note (the docs warn that kept without a note is not a validation).
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: One mark, one gesture, one sound
what: A mark (an arrow, a tick, a ring) is one continuous soft felt glide from the pose where it starts to the pose where it ends.
when: On every mark drawn on the paper.
why: One arrow heard as a burst of little pen strokes (a felt chunk per pose) was refused.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: The paper's own sounds
what: The sheet lands with sheet_in under the pack's whoosh; what moves on it sounds on its poses: the pack's click on a landing, ptick while it settles.
when: On every paper plate.
why: Asked for satisfying sounds when the sheet arrives and what moves on it.

name: The SFX pack, one role each
what: Flash on a change of shot, click on what appears, whoosh into the paper, glitch on one text pop, riser ending on the payoff word.
when: Always; nothing else without the user's ask (no sound per headline word, no hit after the riser).
why: Asked to use the pack: the flash for a change of shot, the paper as a transition, clicks for what appears.
doc: plugins/video/references/audio-spec.md § The SFX pack on the vertical short (2026-09-29, v5)

name: Synthesised taps, shutter and metallic hits
what: The old little synthesised noises, the shutter, the impacts and the pens.
when: Never. The SFX pack replaced them.
why: No little synthesised noises; no metallic hit.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Flash on a change of shot
what: The picture blows out to 0.82 white (up 0.075 s, hold 0.045 s, down 0.095 s) with the pack's camera flash, the cut hidden under the white.
when: On a change of framing, not on every jump cut (that would be a strobe).

name: Motionix light sounds
what: Light sounds for what moves over the speaker, 14-21 LU under the programme, thinned near a whoosh, the flash, the glitch or a riser's end.
when: On what appears over the speaker; the paper keeps the pack's click.
doc: plugins/video/references/audio-spec.md § The light sounds of what appears: the Motionix pack

name: Music bed from the shelf
what: A shelf track mapped once (tempo, sections, drops), aligned on a word, with the house end (low-pass sweep and fade into the cut), about 15 LU under the voice.
when: Every short; the user picks the track in the first question.
why: Asked louder even after the louder version; the landscape level (33 LU under) is far too quiet for a short.

name: Old-radio hook
what: The voice through an old radio set (am) and the picture in an old CRT TV, on the hook only, gone under the flash.
when: A bonus asked in the first question every time, never on by default; around 7 s, never past 10 s.
why: Asked as an option; the radio once ran to 14.9 s and was far too long.

name: Super 8 and VHS looks on the hook
what: Other old looks for the hook: washed Super 8 at 12 fps with dust, or VHS with a tracking band and PLAY.
when: Only in the comparison reels on "let me compare"; crt is the pick.
why: Compared; the reviewer picked crt. Status of film and vhs beyond the comparison not written in the docs.

name: Paper countdown at the end
what: The countdown on scraps of the plates' paper stuck on the jacket, one piece a beat of the music, a pile that grows.
when: At the end of the short.
why: The end speaks the paper.
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Next video taped on a sheet
what: The next video as a print taped on a sheet that drops over the cut, with a yellow NEXT EPISODE sticker and its key words underlined in red marker.
when: At the end, after the countdown.

name: Dark stage at the end
what: Style 4's dark stage, a black-glass countdown and a dark generic at the end.
when: Never. The end speaks the paper.
why: « beaucoup trop différent… on est sur un fond [papier] d'habitude ».
doc: SKILL.md § The vertical language › What was decided

name: Pipecorn generic
what: About 6 s at the very end: Pipecorn, its values replacing one another in one slot, then Pipecorn again, no music; added after the render.
when: A bonus asked every time, never on by default.

name: Your voice made better
what: ElevenLabs' voice isolator takes the room's echo and the noise out of the take before the edit.
when: A bonus asked every time, never on by default; needs the ElevenLabs key.

name: Bottom captions and karaoke
what: The bottom clean captions and the karaoke captions of the older layout.
when: Never unless asked; headlines at the top replaced them.
why: Clean captions judged timid; karaoke rejected as noisy on a talking head.

name: Verbatim words on screen
what: The speaker's words are on screen for the whole short, never rewritten or translated; a word may be dropped for room and the delivery says which.
when: Always.
why: LinkedIn autoplays muted; the first run came back translated and every cue hung on words never said.

name: Times on measured word onsets
what: Every time in the plan is a word onset moved onto the voice's attack, and a real end before a pause, measured on the envelope.
when: Always; never a round number picked by feel.
why: The transcript puts words in the silence before them and ends phrases early (0.34 s on the reference take).

name: Bullet lists on screen
what: A list of points on screen, like a slide.
when: Never.
why: Every one was rejected.
doc: SKILL.md § 2. Read the transcript and decide the pictures

name: Real names and real numbers only
what: Logos, product screens and figures are the user's real ones; a beat without the real number is cut.
when: Always.
why: Every number on screen is a claim a viewer can check.

name: The macOS product demo
what: The screen wakes, the dock icon bounces, the app opens and the product builds inside it, then the window is pushed forward until it is the full-frame card.
when: For a product demo, with the user's own wallpaper and data.
why: Status not written in the docs.
doc: SKILL.md § 2. Read the transcript and decide the pictures

name: The map
what: A map of nodes read from the project's own gtmos-nodes.json, drawn as the product builds.
when: For a product demo, with the user's own data, never invented content.
why: Status not written in the docs.
doc: SKILL.md § 2. Read the transcript and decide the pictures

name: Feed safe zones
what: Every text and important element stays inside x 0.095-0.905, y 0.128-0.774; never the bottom band (y 0.79 and below) or under the buttons (x 0.84 and right, from y 0.425).
when: Always; on a tight shot the words go below the head.

name: Loudness at -14 LUFS
what: The mix ends at -14 LUFS with a true-peak ceiling of -1.0 dBTP, by ffmpeg's two-pass loudnorm, verified numerically.
when: Always; never a bare volume gain.
doc: plugins/video/references/audio-spec.md § Loudness: a standard, not a taste

name: Never regrade the footage
what: The source's colour, bit depth and HDR tags pass through unchanged; HDR to SDR is opt-in only.
when: Always.
why: The first assembly that shipped an HDR to SDR conversion unasked came straight back.

name: Rush assembled by breath groups
what: A long take with restarts is cut into one clean take, choosing the good attempt by reading and cutting only at measured pauses between breath groups.
when: When the source is a rush, before the edit; the keep list is proposed to the user first.
why: A silence threshold keeps all attempts; whisper's word ends clipped the last syllable of 23 of 40 segments.

name: Pace measured against the published version
what: The speed of a derushed file is measured by matching its audio envelope to the published short.
when: When a published version of the take exists; measure before assuming x1.
why: On the reference short it was 10 % slower than published.

name: Landscape title lockup
what: A stacked lockup of three to five short lines in Satoshi Black with a serif accent and the payoff in yellow, left or right of the head, on the under layer.
when: In landscape mode, the intro of a long 16:9 video.
why: Validated on a real video over five review rounds.

name: Lateral slide
what: At constant zoom only the anchor travels, in 0.34 s, moving the frame sideways.
when: In landscape mode; it was asked for more.

name: Many zooms in landscape
what: Movement on the zoom axis beyond the five argument punches.
when: Never; a punch only on the yellow word of the five beats that carry the argument.
why: Rejected three times: too many zooms.

name: Landscape figures: count, hero, chips, heard scroll
what: A number that climbs, one enormous glyph rising from behind the speaker, real logos coming out from behind, and a scroll heard as one click per row.
when: In landscape mode, one library sound per beat.
why: Status not written in the docs, beyond landscape mode being validated as a whole.

name: Captions in another language as natural phrases
what: Text in the user's language over speech in another one is written as natural 3-6 word phrases anchored on the source word's onset, not word chunks translated one by one.
when: In landscape mode when the on-screen language differs from the audio.
why: Captions that read translated were a review note.
